chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Basie advises Fields not to go home
summary: Basie tells Fields Alexander will look out for him and not to return to Oklahoma.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Anyway, Basie and I had a talk and I told Basie I think I'll head back to Oklahoma and the Count said why. I said they don't have any work for me, so he said he thinks an awful lot of your band, Fields, he said I wouldn't go back if I were you. I said I don't like to be in that position. He said Alexander is going to look out for you, and I said what do you mean? He said, do you see that luggage down in the basement where you all rehearse, with Count Basie on? I said yeah. He said I had to leave them here six months, a year ago for room. He said a man had been double paid and

I bought new, I don't need it, and he said I was behind then but I stayed here and Willard knew that he was responsible for me. He said now if you go back to Oklahoma (inaudible), he's not going to be responsible, and so I said to him, I already owe Alexander about four hundred dollars for the uniforms that he got us. He said, has he asked you for it? I said no. He knows you're not working. He said, you start worrying when he starts worrying; if he's not worrying, don't worry.
